title: Move the 16 not-attempted client-test stubs onto the shared fake (LIN-4255 leftovers)
description:
Follow-up to LIN-4252 and LIN-4255. **Rewritten in the LIN-4255 close-out** (the earlier text described LIN-4252's 18 `makeContainer` files; LIN-4255 has since moved most of them onto the shared fake).

## Problem

16 test files still hand-write a single-element stub for a `public/` client script. They are on `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` in `tests/unit/fake-dom-census.test.js`, so the census ratchet keeps them listed and nothing can add to the list. None was attempted by LIN-4255: no move piece of its approved plan covered them (LIN-4255 plan-review note 1b), so they were dropped from that ticket and routed here. They are not stopped. Each is a single-element stub that the shared fake (`tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`, with `tests/unit/helpers/client-world.js` `loadWorld` over it) can serve as it stands.

## The 16 files (all under `tests/unit/`)

Pre-move checks first (verify once when the file is moved):

* `run-limit-gating.test.js`: `querySelector` returns null (line 121). Its moved path reaches the `querySelector ?` guards in LIN-4292.
* `runner-link-surfaces.test.js`: same stub (line 169). `style` is written only on the animation path (`public/swipe.js:534-551`), which this suite does not reach. Verify once.
* `lin-4024-home-description.test.js`: `public/app.js:169` and `:427` write `style.display`. Confirm they are off the description path.
* `lin-3975-proposal-refresh.test.js`: confirm the `idInput` / `questionInput` hooks are `<input>` / `<textarea>` (`public/task-chat.js:35-36`).

Others (12), feasible with the modelled APIs:

* `close-out-client.test.js`
* `dashboard-routes.test.js`
* `lin-2122-history-outcome-pill.test.js`
* `lin-2370-browser-copy-prompt-provider-identity.test.js`
* `lin-3254-session-run-toggles.test.js`
* `lin-4016-sessions-fold-parked.test.js`
* `lin-4024-look.test.js`
* `lin-4242-waiting-live.test.js`
* `question-card-task-bound.test.js`
* `task-page-client.test.js`
* `task-page-link-client-surfaces.test.js`
* `task-page-question.test.js`

## Not in this ticket

The 9 census entries stopped on an API the fake does not model (`style` / `getBoundingClientRect`, `<select>.value`, real bubbling `dispatchEvent`) stay on the list with their stop reason in the census comments. Removing the `querySelector` guards in `public/` is LIN-4292.

## Acceptance

* Each moved file leaves `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` in the same change and joins the `fake-dom.js` header's consumer list.
* Each moved suite keeps its test names and counts (diff sorted test names on base and branch). A test that goes red on the real DOM is reported as a finding, not loosened.
* A file that turns out to need a stop API stays on the list with a comment naming the API and `file:line`.
* `fake-dom-census.test.js` and `claude-md-line-budget.test.js` stay green; the count on the list only falls.

## Method

One family per PR, by the grouping above, as LIN-4255 did: assertion map, before/after test names, a mutation showing each load-bearing assertion goes red.

*Note (20:55, from LIN-4304): when* `close-out-client.test.js` *moves, remove the* `typeof … === 'function'` *seams in* `public/close-out.js` *(around 159/161/175) and their entries in LIN-4304's allow-list.*

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Both Surveys (on this ticket, 20:28–20:29, at `b581ac926`) found the premise understated. "A single-element stub the shared fake can serve as it stands" is not what these 16 files are:

* **None of the 16 uses** `loadWorld`**.** Each builds its own `vm` sandbox, so every move is two moves.
* **Five files hold more than one shape.**
* **The shapes are of three kinds:**
  * **argument seams** (an object handed to a pure function), which are cheap;
  * **document routers** (`querySelector(sel)` mapped to hand-made objects), where each move means writing page markup;
  * **auto-vivifiers** (every selector returns an element: `runner-link-surfaces`, `task-page-link-client-surfaces`, the `Proxy` in `lin-4024-home-description`), which run whole page inits as no-ops. Stops will surface in those.

Here is the person's scope call (big moves early, in pieces, in sequence, since every piece edits the census list):

0. **Probe and derive first, as one piece.**
   * **Tag every flagged shape** as a seam, a router or an auto-vivifier, in the PR.
   * **Probe the three auto-vivifiers** on `loadWorld` with an empty body and record what throws (for example `app.js:1679`'s `insertAdjacentHTML('afterend')`, and `swipe.js`'s style and layout). That resizes the ticket before any move.
   * **Make the census derive and assert the fake's consumer list.** The header names every real importer of `fake-dom.js`/`client-world.js`, and the census checks it. The hand-kept paragraph then can't drift by 16 names during this ticket. This item moves here from LIN-4297, so the moves don't hand-edit that list 16 times.
1. **Then one group per client script,** each its own PR, in this order:
   1. sessions/app (`lin-3254`, `lin-4016-sessions-fold-parked`, both `lin-4024`);
   2. `common.js` slices (`lin-2370`, `lin-4242-waiting-live`, and the one client test in `dashboard-routes`);
   3. question-cards (`question-card-task-bound`);
   4. swipe/prompt-section (`runner-link-surfaces`, `task-page-link-client-surfaces`, `run-limit-gating`, `lin-2122`);
   5. task-page (`task-page-client`, `task-page-question`, `lin-3975-proposal-refresh`, and `close-out-client` last).
2. **"Moved" means on** `loadWorld`**.** Delete each file's private `vm` sandbox. Don't wrap it around the fake. For a script loaded as a slice (`lin-2122`, `lin-3254`, `dashboard-routes`), use `loadWorld({ scripts: [] })` plus `world.run`, as LIN-4284 did.
3. **Router markup comes from the server's real renderer** where one exists, not from hand-written HTML, or the fixture drifts the way the stub did.
4. **A** `querySelector: () => null` **stub that becomes a real tree brings dead paths to life.** A test that goes red there is a finding. Classify each one (a real client bug, a test that passed vacuously, or a fake gap), as the LIN-4255 pieces did.
5. **Stops: don't widen the fake in this ticket.** A file that hits an API the fake doesn't model stays listed, with that API named. A fake widening is its own ticket, pinned against Chromium as in LIN-4296.
   * The question-cards suites avoid the bubbling-`dispatchEvent` stop only because `loadWorld` supplies no `CustomEvent`. Say so in a comment in each, in the present tense.
   * Whether the fake models bubbling `dispatchEvent` is a separate decision, for the notebook.
6. `close-out-client` **goes last, after LIN-4304 has merged.** Removing `public/close-out.js`'s `typeof … === 'function'` seams is a production change, made as its own step. It also removes their entries from LIN-4304's allow-list.
7. **Test names:**
   * Every moved test keeps its name.
   * A test may move to a better-placed suite. The `dashboard-routes` client test is a server suite's only client test, so move it to a client suite and don't make `dashboard-routes` import `client-world.js`.
   * A new case may join an existing suite.
   * The PR maps every name. **Don't split a file just to keep a count:** LIN-4296's `lin-4296-scope-pick` copied its parent's fixture to do that.

**Not this ticket:** modelling bubbling `dispatchEvent`, `style` or layout in the fake; the `typeof CustomEvent` guard in `question-cards.js`.

## At merge (each piece)

* The census falls by the number moved, and each remaining entry's reason is true now.
* The derived consumer list is green.
* Every red-then-classified test is listed.
* The full unit suite passes.

## Implementation Plan

*Revised after the Plan Review Verdict (20:39), which asked for changes. Planned at* `b581ac92` *(= main HEAD; re-checked: nothing under* `tests/unit/` *or* `public/` *has landed since). Built on the two Survey comments (20:28, 20:29) and the review, whose line references were re-read against the code.*

**What changed in this revision, and which finding each answers:**

* Finding 1 (blocking, `dashboard-routes` had no fixture to move with): Piece 2 now starts with a pure extraction of the route fixture into a shared module, then moves the badge test to a named new client suite.
* Finding 2 (empty-body probe fails on setup gaps): Piece 0's probe now runs with the suite's own window stubs and the renderer's markup, and says which failures count as stop reasons.
* Finding 3 (`loadWorld` has no markup option): Piece 4 now says swipe-loading suites use `scripts: []` + `parse` + `world.run`.
* Finding 4 (derived consumer list): taken the second way the review offered. The header stops naming consumers and the census computes them, so the moves never edit it. `lin-4293` and the LIN-4297 wording are handled.
* Finding 5 (`close-out.js:187`): decided, removed in the same production commit.
* Finding 6 (relation on a closed ticket): a follow-up ticket, not a relation.
* Finding 7 (grouping labels): agreed, labels corrected; order kept because it only matters for census conflicts.
* Baseline count corrected to 573 (the 16 files, `fake-dom-census` and `claude-md-line-budget`).

### What this is for, and what done looks like

16 client suites still carry a private `vm` sandbox and hand-made stub elements, so they sit on `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` and every new witness in them is cheap to write wrongly (a stub returning `null` for every lookup keeps whole code paths dead). Done = each of the 16 either (a) runs on `loadWorld`/`createFakeDom` with its private sandbox deleted and its entry gone from the census list, or (b) stays on the list with a comment naming the stop API with `file:line`. The list only falls; test names are preserved (diff of sorted names, base vs branch, in each PR); a test that goes red on the real tree is reported as a classified finding, never loosened.

*Done-when is the ticket's Acceptance section, with one change: "joins the* `fake-dom.js` *header's consumer list" is dropped, because Piece 0 makes the consumer list computed (its reason: the ticket's own scope call wants the moves not to hand-edit that list 16 times). The ticket text "single-element stub the fake serves as it stands" is wrong (Survey, re-confirmed: none of the 16 uses* `loadWorld`*; 5 files hold several shapes; 3 are auto-vivifiers); the plan is built on the Survey's version.*

### Facts re-read at HEAD (where they differ from the ticket prose)

* `run-limit-gating`'s pre-check is moot: LIN-4292 landed (`b389f9b0`); its stub (`:121`) is a plain `querySelector() { return null; }` and it moves like the others.
* The census holds 22 entries: 6 with stop comments, and our 16 are exactly the ones without.
* `close-out.js` seams: `:158-161` and `:174-175` (`typeof d.querySelector`, `typeof main.getAttribute`, `typeof d.querySelectorAll`) plus `:187` (`typeof box.appendChild`). Re-read the lines when LIN-4304 lands.
* LIN-4304 is In Progress, not merged. The `close-out-client` step is blocked on it.
* `app.js:1679` `insertAdjacentHTML('afterend')` exists and the fake throws on non-`beforeend`; it runs only on a `.dispatch-disclosure-placeholder`. `app.js:169,427` write `this.style.display`; the fake does not model `style`. `click()` is called at `app.js:71`, `app.js:2010` and `prompt-section.js:2612`; the fake deliberately has no `click`.
* `question-cards.js:236` returns when `typeof CustomEvent !== 'function'`; `loadWorld` supplies no `CustomEvent`, so `question-card-task-bound`, `task-page-question` and `lin-4242-waiting-live` avoid the bubbling-`dispatchEvent` stop only by that absence.
* `loadWorld` has no `markup` option (that is LIN-4289/LIN-4297 item 1, not on main). A script that queries the DOM at load (`swipe.js:84`) needs its markup parsed in before it runs.
* The `fake-dom.js` header's consumer paragraph already misses `lin-4293-tidy-after-repaint.test.js`, which imports `client-world.js` (`:18`).
* `lin-3975`'s hooks are read through `root.querySelector('[data-task-chat="id"|"question"]')` (`task-chat.js:33-37`); whether they are `<input>`/`<textarea>` is a markup fact the builder confirms from the server renderer.

### Direction and what was set aside

Move **by client script**, one PR per group, in sequence (every PR edits the census list, so they cannot land in parallel), with a probe-and-derive piece first. "Moved" means on `loadWorld` with the private `vm.createContext` deleted. Set aside: wrapping each sandbox around the fake (keeps 16 second loaders); widening the fake (separate ticket, pinned against Chromium as in LIN-4296); modelling bubbling `dispatchEvent`; splitting a file to preserve a count; copying a fixture; replacing a real route with a canned payload; making `dashboard-routes` import `client-world.js`.

### Piece 0 — probe and derive (lands first, alone)

1. **Tag every flagged shape** in the 16 files as seam / router / auto-vivifier, in the PR description (a table, not code). Starting point: auto-vivifiers `runner-link-surfaces:184`, `task-page-link-client-surfaces:47`, `lin-4024-home-description:70`; routers `task-page-client:328/399`, `task-page-question:221-253`, `lin-3975:157`; seams `close-out-client` boxes and `task-page-client:415`.
2. **Probe the three auto-vivifiers** on `loadWorld` (scratch only, not committed), **with the window stubs each suite already passes and the markup the server's renderer produces**, not an empty body. An empty body fails on setup gaps (`app.js` throws `window.addEventListener is not a function`; `swipe.js:84` queries `.swipe-filter-select` at load and `:943` calls `addEventListener` on the null), which say nothing about the fake. **Only these count as a stop reason:** a `FakeDomError`, a `style` or layout read, or a call to an unmodelled method (`click()` included). Output: per file, moves / stays listed with the API and `file:line`. This resizes pieces 1 and 4 before any move.
3. **The census computes the fake's consumers; the header stops hand-keeping them.** The `fake-dom.js` header's consumer paragraph is replaced by a sentence saying the consumers are the importers the census computes (keep `helpers/client-world.js` and `helpers/live-console-world.js` described as real importers, and keep the sentence naming `fake-dom-census.test.js` as the guard; that file imports nothing, so it is not a consumer). The census computes the real importers of `fake-dom.js`/`client-world.js` (a repeatable import scan over `tests/`, same scope as its AST scan, which already finds `lin-4293`) and fails if the header again hand-lists a consumer file name. Behaviour and witness: a fixture test where a header that lists a consumer file goes red, and one where the pointer sentence stands goes green, plus the real run green on main. Remove the "joins the consumer list" instruction from the census stale-file message (`:648-649`) and from the header's last sentence of that paragraph; every later PR then edits only `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES`. *Reason for this reading:* the other reading (header names every importer, census checks) keeps the hand step in all 16 moves and starts red on main (`lin-4293`).
4. **LIN-4297:** comment that this item moved here, and that its Done-when "No hand-kept consumer list remains" is now met by Piece 0, so LIN-4297 must not delete what Piece 0 builds.

### Pieces 1–5 (one PR each, in this order; each is a group)

For every piece: delete each file's private sandbox; use `loadWorld`; slices and top-level-querying scripts use `loadWorld({ scripts: [] })` + `parse(markup, document.body)` + `world.run(source)` (as `observation-ruling-delivery` and LIN-4284 do; still "on `loadWorld`", not a wrapped sandbox); router markup comes from the server's real renderer where one exists, not hand-written HTML; `querySelector: () => null` stubs become real trees, so a newly red test is classified (real client bug / vacuous pass / fake gap) and listed in the PR; a file that hits an API the fake does not model stays listed with the API and `file:line` in its census comment. Each PR carries: assertion map, before/after sorted test names, and one mutation per load-bearing assertion showing it goes red. Each PR runs `fake-dom-census`, `claude-md-line-budget` and the full unit suite.

1. **sessions/app**: `lin-3254` (loads `session.js`, sliced by `indexOf`), `lin-4016-sessions-fold-parked`, `lin-4024-look`, `lin-4024-home-description`. Stop candidate: `lin-4024-home-description` (`app.js:1679` only if its path reaches a `.dispatch-disclosure-placeholder`; `app.js:169/427` `style`); Piece 0's probe decides.
2. `common.js` **slices**: `lin-2370`, `lin-4242-waiting-live`, and the client test in `dashboard-routes` (`:6858-6878`: "the badge paints the page's own workspace number when a second workspace holds a ruling"). Note `common.js` throws at load without `__HARNESS_MODELS__` (`client-world.js` header). `lin-4242-waiting-live` loads `question-cards.js`: keep `CustomEvent` absent and say so in a present-tense comment.
   * **First commit: a pure extraction.** Move the route fixture the badge test needs out of `dashboard-routes.test.js` into one shared module (for example `tests/fixtures/dashboard-router.js`, builder's name): `makeStores` (`:55`), `findRouteLayer`/`getHandler` (`:110/:127`), `makeReqRes` (`:132`), `makeRouter` (`:148`), `decisionItem` (`:325`) and the `withDefaults` wrapper (`:32`) with what they import. The module holds no `test()` calls, so importing it runs no tests. `dashboard-routes` imports it back. Witness: sorted test names and the pass count of `dashboard-routes` identical before and after, and the file still does not import `client-world.js`. Take only what the other 256 tests also use into the module, leaving single-use helpers in place, and say which in the PR.
   * **Second commit: the move.** The badge test goes to a **new** client suite (none covers `updateRulingsBadge` today; only e2e specs do; builder names it, e.g. after LIN-4103), importing the fixture module plus `loadWorld({ scripts: [] })` and `world.run(slice)`. The real route's JSON feeds the real sliced function; the stub `badge`/`countEl` become real elements. Name preserved; the name map in the PR records old file → new file. `dashboard-routes`' census entry goes when the hand-made fake leaves it. Mutation: make the client read `count` instead of `workspaceCount` and the test goes red; also rename `workspaceCount` in the route and see it red (this is what a canned payload would have lost).
3. **question-cards**: `question-card-task-bound`. Replace stub `.click()`/`card.removed` with `clickOn`/`isConnected` (the assertion map changes here and the PR says so); same `CustomEvent` comment.
4. **swipe / prompt-section / dispatch slice**: `runner-link-surfaces` (loads `swipe.js`), `task-page-link-client-surfaces` (loads `swipe.js`), `run-limit-gating` (loads `prompt-section.js`), `lin-2122-history-outcome-pill` (slices `dispatch.js` by `indexOf`; `scripts: []` + `world.run`). The two swipe loaders parse the page markup first, then run `swipe.js`. Piece 0's probe decides whether they move or stay listed; expect at least `task-page-link-client-surfaces` to be a stop candidate (`swipe.js` has 26 `style`/layout hits; the ticket listed it as "feasible" in error).
5. **task-page**: `task-page-client`, `task-page-question` (same `CustomEvent` comment), `lin-3975-proposal-refresh`, then `close-out-client` **last, only after LIN-4304 has merged**, as two commits in its own PR: first the production change, removing the `typeof … === 'function'` seams in `public/close-out.js` (`:159/:161/:175`) **and** `:187` **(**`typeof box.appendChild`**)**, since `close-out-client`'s boxes become real elements and `appendChild` is outside LIN-4304's method list (so it has no allow-list entry to remove), plus the entries of the others in LIN-4304's allow-list; then the test move. `close-out-client:242` exists to feed those seams hand-made docs, so it needs real markup; test names are kept by re-pointing, not deleting.
   * **If LIN-4304 has not merged when pieces 1–4 are done:** `close-out-client` stays on the list and this ticket closes with it named as the one remainder. At that point (not before) file a **follow-up ticket** for the `close-out-client` move plus the seam removal, marked blocked-by LIN-4304, and link it from LIN-4254's closing comment. A relation on a closed LIN-4254 would hide the leftover.

### How we know we've found every place

The 16 are exactly the census entries without a stop comment (re-derivable: `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` lines with no `// stop:`); the census scan is the catch-all for any other hand-written fake and fails both ways. Other places the behaviour lives: the `fake-dom.js` consumer list (now computed, so there is nothing to find), the stop comments on remaining entries (each must be true at merge), and `public/` seams shaped around stubs. Those are **out of scope** (LIN-4292 done; LIN-4304 for the `typeof` seams, with the `close-out.js` ones coupled to Piece 5). `CLAUDE.md` needs no change (re-read: it says only "use the fake"); `claude-md-line-budget.test.js` runs each PR.

### Likeliest ways it breaks

1. A formerly-dead path comes alive on the real tree and the test fails, or passes for a different reason. Witness: one mutation per load-bearing assertion, and the sorted-names diff; red tests are findings, not loosened.
2. An auto-vivifier hits a fake gap (`style`, `afterend`, layout, `click`) mid-move and the pull is to widen the fake or wrap the old stub. Witness: Piece 0's probe decides first, with the stop-reason rule above; the census (no stale entries) and an unchanged `fake-dom.test.js` catch a quiet widening.
3. The Piece 2 extraction changes `dashboard-routes` by accident (a helper's behaviour or import order shifts). Witness: identical sorted names and pass count, and the rename mutation above.
4. The question-cards suites reach the bubbling-`dispatchEvent` stop if anything gives the sandbox a `CustomEvent`. Witness: the present-tense comment in each, and the suites staying green on `loadWorld` defaults.

### Guards touched

None loosened: the census list only falls and each removal is enforced by the stale-entry check; Piece 0 *adds* a check (and drops a hand-kept paragraph the old check never enforced). The one production edit (`close-out.js` seams) is gated behind LIN-4304 and removes a guard that existed only for stubs, with its own test move as witness.

### Session fit and review

needs multiple sessions — six PRs (Piece 0 plus groups 1–5), sequential because each edits the census list, each verified on its own, and the last gated on LIN-4304. Build it as sequential dispatches or sub-tickets in that order.

plan-review due: yes (needs more than one session, Piece 5 touches production code behind another ticket, and this revision changed Piece 0's contract and Piece 2's shape).

### Relations to record

None now. A step cannot carry a relation. The only one needed is the follow-up ticket blocked-by LIN-4304, created if the ticket closes before LIN-4304 merges (see Piece 5). The LIN-4297 note is a comment, made in Piece 0.

Type label: Improvement (nearest in the catalog; no test-infra label exists). LIN-4252 merged as d234b94a; the shared fake now models `type` and `checked` too.

Rewritten in the LIN-4255 close-out (review comment cb4cbff9, ledger item 1): the description now lists exactly the 16 census entries LIN-4255 never attempted, with the 4 pre-move checks, instead of LIN-4252 18 makeContainer files (most already moved). Priority unchanged (Low).

## Survey global: LIN-4254 @ b581ac926

**Where it lands.** `tests/unit/`: 16 client suites, `fake-dom-census.test.js` (22 entries at base, 6 with stop comments, 16 without), and the header of `helpers/fake-dom.js`. It is improving fast: the census went from 56 to 22 over 13 PRs on 2026-11-05, against a list enforced both ways. Meanwhile `fake-dom.js` reached 1054 lines, and its header's consumer list is a ~25-line paragraph nothing checks; the census only *tells* you to update it (census :648-649).

**What the obvious move does.** Each file is really two moves, not one. None of the 16 uses `loadWorld`: each builds its own `vm.createContext` sandbox (2–7 vm calls per file). So the task also retires 16 private copies of `client-world.js`; wrapping each sandbox around the fake instead would keep a second loader in every file. Three suites load a *slice* of a script rather than the whole file: `lin-2122` and `lin-3254` slice by `indexOf`, and `dashboard-routes` slices `updateRulingsBadge` at :6860. `loadWorld({ scripts: [] })` + `world.run` already covers this (precedent: `task-chat-flight-companion-sentinel-mask`, LIN-4284).

"Single-element stub" understates some of these:
- `question-card-task-bound` builds a whole card by regex over the rendered markup, with a `querySelector` switch and a hand-rolled `click()` (:46-97). The fake has no `click()`, so this one needs `clickOn`.
- `querySelector: () => null` appears in at least six files, not just the two the ticket flags. On a real tree those lookups *succeed*, so code paths that were dead in these tests come alive. Expect red tests that are findings.
- `dashboard-routes` is a 6910-line server-route suite with 257 tests. Its only fake is in one test that pipes a handler's JSON into a client slice. Moved in place, it becomes the only server suite importing `client-world.js`.
- `question-card-task-bound`, `task-page-question` and `lin-4242-waiting-live` load `question-cards.js`, whose bubbling `dispatchEvent` (:235-244) stopped three other suites. They miss it only because no `CustomEvent` is in the sandbox (`typeof CustomEvent` guard). Keep it that way, or they reach the stop.

**Who has to learn about it.** The census list is enforced. The header consumer list is not, and will drift silently by 16 names. CLAUDE.md needs no change. `public/close-out.js` has 4 `typeof … === 'function'` seams, and `common.js` and `prompt-section.js` have one each. Those exist *because* the stubs were partial.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry.**
1. Have the census compute the actual importers of `fake-dom.js`/`client-world.js` and assert that the header names each one.
2. Delete each file's private sandbox outright rather than adapting it, so "moved" means "on `loadWorld`", not just "uses `createFakeDom`".

**Better still, not this task's.** The ticket is aimed at a number; the deeper symptom is that `public/` carries seams shaped around test stubs (the `typeof` guards, the `querySelector ?` guards in LIN-4292, the `typeof CustomEvent` early-return). This task is the precondition for removing them, so LIN-4292/LIN-4304 should follow family by family rather than wait for all 16. Separately, whether `fake-dom.js` should model bubbling `dispatchEvent` decides the last 3 stopped suites; that decision is bigger than this ticket.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4254 @ b581ac926

Read in a worktree at `b581ac926`. The 16 suites plus the census pass at base (571/571).

**The premise is the hard part.** The ticket says each file is "a single-element stub the shared fake can serve as it stands." A scratch run of the census with an empty list shows 5 files hold more than one shape: `task-page-client` 7, `close-out-client` 3, and `lin-4242-waiting-live`, `task-page-link-client-surfaces` and `task-page-question` 2 each. Most shapes are not elements. There are three kinds:

1. **Argument seams**, where a pure function is handed an object (`close-out-client`'s boxes, `task-page-client:415`). These are cheap to convert with `createFakeDom` + `parse`.
2. **Document routers**, where `querySelector(sel)` maps to hand-made objects (`task-page-client:328/399`, `task-page-question:221-253`, `lin-3975:157`). The real fake returns null unless the markup exists, so each move means writing page markup. That is fixture authoring, not a swap.
3. **Auto-vivifiers**, where every selector returns an element: `el(sel)` in `runner-link-surfaces:184` and `task-page-link-client-surfaces:47`, and a `Proxy` over the whole document and window in `lin-4024-home-description:70`. They run whole page inits (`app.js`, `swipe.js` + `common.js`) where every write is a no-op. On the fake those paths go live, and that is where stop APIs will surface, not where the pre-checks look:
   - `task-page-link-client-surfaces` loads `swipe.js` (26 `style`/layout hits) and stubs `style: {}`, yet sits in the "feasible" 12.
   - `app.js:1679` uses `insertAdjacentHTML('afterend')`, which the fake throws on.

`question-card-task-bound` asserts through stub `.click()` and `card.removed`, so its assertion map changes (to `clickOn`/`isConnected`). Its card matches the `dispatchEvent`-stopped shape. It is safe only because `announceRulingGone` (`question-cards.js:236`) exits without `CustomEvent`, which `loadWorld` doesn't supply.

**Stale wording.**
- LIN-4292 already landed (`b389f9b0`, before base: "unblocks no test suite"), so the `run-limit-gating` pre-check is moot.
- The census lists 6 stops, not 9.
- LIN-4304's allow-list isn't on main. Removing the `typeof` seams at `close-out.js:158-159,174` is a production change, and it collides with "keep test names and counts": `close-out-client:242` exists to feed those seams hand-made docs. Do that removal after LIN-4304 lands, as its own step.

**Grouping.** "Family by the grouping above" yields 4 pre-checks and 12 others, not families. Group by client script:
- task-page (`task-page-client`, `task-page-question`, `lin-3975`, `close-out-client`)
- question-cards
- `common.js` slices (`dashboard-routes`, which is one test at :6878 in a 6,910-line suite, `lin-4242-waiting-live`, `lin-2370`)
- sessions/app (`lin-3254`, `lin-4016`, both `lin-4024`)
- swipe/prompt-section (`runner-link`, `task-page-link`, `run-limit-gating`, `lin-2122`)

**First:**
1. Tag every flagged shape as seam, router or auto-vivifier.
2. Probe the three auto-vivifiers on `loadWorld` with an empty body and see what throws. They are the likeliest to stay on the list, and knowing early resizes the ticket.
3. Decide where router markup comes from. Prefer the server's real renderer over hand-written HTML, or the fixture drifts the way the stub did.
